title: Prefill Heuristic Factory and Quant Snapshotter: automated prefill defaults + lightweight quant snapshots
author: Evan Li
release_notes: Adds a new prefill heuristic factory (auto-select defaults for batch/cache/quant) and a compact quant snapshot format for faster rollout; safe rollout with canary flag and no customer-visible API changes.
description: Context: Many tenants still rely on hand-tuned prefill/batching/cache defaults or per-tenant quant profiles. This causes slow onboarding and conservative defaults that cost more tokens. Motivation: automate sensible, conservative defaults for prefill/batching/caching and provide a small, immutable quant snapshot format that can be applied as a fallback during rollouts. What this PR does: introduces a Prefill Heuristic Factory that synthesizes tenant defaults from lightweight workload fingerprints + historical latency/cost signals, and a Quant Snapshotter that produces compact, versioned quantization metadata (quant-snapshot.v1) for safe, fast rollouts. Key properties: (1) conservative by default — suggested defaults never increase tokenization time or KV cache pressure beyond configured SLOs; (2) explainable — heuristics output human-readable rationale strings for Console and CLI; (3) snapshotable — quant snapshots are signed, small (~3-10KB), and include fallback links to the original model artifact. Implementation summary: - runtime/prefill: new heuristics factory module (pkg/prefill/factory.go) with a plugin interface to add tenant-specific rules; includes a deterministic rule set: warmup-window heuristic, microbatch preference, prefix-cache aggressiveness scaler. - control-plane: prefill service API to compute and cache tenant defaults (api/prefill/v1). - quant: snapshotter utility (tools/quant/snapshotter.py) that reads model metrics and writes signed quant-snapshot.v1 YAML; small loader in runtime (pkg/quant/snapshot_loader.go) that validates signature and exposes on-disk cache. - telemetry: new metrics (prefill.suggested_defaults, prefill.apply_count, quant.snapshot_applied) and Console change to show rationale. Migration / rollout: default behavior is opt-in via tenant flag; admin CLI can dry-run suggestions and export JSON to policy-as-code. We run a staged rollout: dry-run -> canary (5 tenants) -> broad apply. Testing: unit tests for heuristics and snapshot format, integration tests in CI that validate safety gates (latency regression < 2% in synthetic workloads), and a small e2e against the local quickstart environment. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes. Ops notes: when enabling on Dedicated/Private, customers must provide model artifact access for snapshot validation. Related: ENG-2145 (prefill heuristics), ENG-2146 (quant snapshot pipeline).

review_comments: Maya Chen: Please add a short circuit to skip suggestion for tenants with explicit policy lock. -> Author: added a lock check in api/prefill/v1/service.go

Arjun Patel: The microbatch heuristic seems aggressive for ultra-low-latency tenants; can we make it tenant-weighted? -> Author: converted the scalar into a tenant-weighted multiplier and added a config flag (prefill.microbatch_max_scale)
Simone Ruiz: The snapshot signature uses HMAC; can we support asymmetric signatures for customer HSMs? -> Author: added an optional X.509 signature path and documented it in snapshotter README
Maya Chen (follow-up): Add more unit tests for signature failure modes. -> Author: added two negative tests and a CI step to validate corrupted snapshots are rejected

notes_for_oncall: If tenants report unexpected latency increases after enabling suggestions, flip the tenant flag to off (cli: redwood prefill set --tenant <id> --enabled=false). Telemetry to watch: prefill.apply_count, request.latency.p90 for the model route, quant.snapshot_applied failures. If signature verification failures are seen, check model artifact access and server clock skew.
manual_test_steps: 4) Load snapshot in runtime: set PREFILL_QUANT_SNAPSHOT=/path/snapshot.v1 and restart inference runtime
